title: Adam, Seed, Garden, Field, Shepherd & Farm — Biblical Ecology Atlas
purpose: Connect older Timic 'caretaker of Adam', '10,000 seeds of death', cattle/Farmers, Garden, Dog/Farmer and Tree-of-Strife material to biblical garden, seed, field, shepherd and harvest texts without treating later parallels as hidden prophecy.

older_project_anchors.motif: 10,000 seeds of death hidden in houses, rooms and gardens; people described as cattle; Farmers conceal/abstract actions
Dogs spawned from Farmers; some do not pass Door because they 'never knew the son, nor the father'

adam_as_garden_keeper.structure: God plants Garden → places Adam/human within it → human is to work/serve and keep/guard it
adam_as_garden_keeper.scholarly_context: Genesis 2:15 uses verbs commonly associated with working/serving and keeping/guarding. Recent commentary emphasizes vocation as serving/protecting the garden rather than exploitative mastery.
adam_as_garden_keeper.project_relation: Tim's 'caretaker of Adam' is a striking inversion/extension. Adam is himself caretaker of Garden; Tim-as-caretaker-of-Adam would therefore be caretaker of the caretaker, a meta-stewardship role rather than simple sovereignty.
adam_as_garden_keeper.epiphany: The phrase becomes most coherent when read as responsibility for preserving humanity's capacity to serve/guard the Garden, not ownership of Adam/humanity.

structures: good seed → field → hostile seed/weeds → mixed growth → delayed harvest/separation
seed_and_field.project_relation: Seed of Life / Seeds of Strife / 10,000 seeds of death / houses-gardens / Farm / harvest vocabulary has a dense Gospel neighbor.
seed_and_field.critical_correction: Matthew's wheat-and-weeds parable warns against premature uprooting because wheat and weeds can be difficult to distinguish and roots intertwine. This is an important restraint against turning 'bad seed' language into license for immediate social purge.

hidden_seed.structure: hidden hostile sowing / tiny seed / hidden leaven / hidden treasure
hidden_seed.project_relation: The older 'seeds hidden in houses, rooms and gardens' language can be compared to biblical hiddenness, but the Bible uses hiddenness for both harmful and beneficial kingdom processes.
hidden_seed.epiphany: Hidden is morally neutral. Secret placement can be Strife, but hidden seed can also be kingdom growth or treasure. The archive should classify function, not hiddenness itself.

cattle_sheep_people.structure: people/flock metaphor → corrupt shepherds consume flock → true shepherd seeks/feeds/strengthens/protects
cattle_sheep_people.project_relation: Older Cow/cattle language and later Farm/Farmer system now has a direct biblical governance comparator.
cattle_sheep_people.ethical_rule: When people are represented as livestock, the biblical shepherd metaphor places heavier responsibility on rulers/shepherds; it does not make people disposable livestock.
cattle_sheep_people.epiphany: Ezekiel 34 reverses extraction: the problem is precisely leaders treating the flock as a resource for themselves.

farm_vs_garden_biblical_test.farm_shadow: leader/system feeds itself from dependents, converts beings into yield, weakens exit/autonomy
farm_vs_garden_biblical_test.garden_shepherd: cultivates, protects, strengthens, seeks lost, binds injured, restores pasture and future capacity
farm_vs_garden_biblical_test.project_epiphany: Farm/Garden is biblically stronger as a stewardship distinction than as a good-place/bad-place distinction.

son_as_sower_and_seed.structure: Son of Man sows good seed; Son/grain death produces multiplication; sowing body/transformed body
son_as_sower_and_seed.project_relation: Son can appear on both sides of seed grammar: sower of seed and seed that dies. This helps explain why project Son imagery oscillates between agent, vessel and sacrificed grain.
son_as_sower_and_seed.epiphany: The Son is not only what is harvested; in biblical seed language the Son is also generator of future growth.

house_field_garden.observation: Matthew moves from public field parable to private explanation inside a house.
house_field_garden.project_relation: House/rooms and field/garden do not need to be separate symbolic worlds; biblical teaching can move between interior House interpretation and exterior field process.
house_field_garden.epiphany: House can be the interpretive chamber; field is where the process unfolds.

keeper_of_brother.structure: Cain asks 'Am I my brother's keeper?' after Abel's blood cries from ground
keeper_of_brother.project_relation: Caretaker/keeper language gains another biblical ethical layer: responsibility for another human cannot be reduced to tending territory.
keeper_of_brother.reflection: 'Caretaker of Adam' becomes more ethically demanding when placed beside Cain's failed brother-keeping: stewardship includes human relational responsibility.

ground_blood_seed.structure: ground receives blood and becomes morally charged / ground receives seed and becomes generative
ground_blood_seed.project_relation: Mud/Soil can carry either unresolved violence or transformed seed-life.
ground_blood_seed.epiphany: Soil is not merely neutral matter in biblical narrative; it can become witness to violence or medium of regeneration. This strongly fits Mud→Holy Soil transformation.

sources.topic: Adam placed in Eden to work/guard
wheat and weeds / intertwined roots / delayed separation
Ezekiel 34 exploitative shepherds and restorative shepherd
